subproblem.title: Uniform convergence of difference quotients of a C^1 map into a normed space
subproblem.statement: Let n be a natural number, E a real normed space, g : R^n -> E, U an open subset of R^n, K a compact subset of R^n with K ⊆ U, and e ∈ R^n. Assume g is C^1 on U. Then the difference quotients d^{-1}(g(x + d e) - g(x)) converge to Dg(x) e (Dg = fderiv) uniformly for x ∈ K as d -> 0 with d ≠ 0, i.e. along the punctured neighbourhood filter 𝓝[≠] 0 of 0 in R.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (g : Rn n → E) (U K : Set (Rn n)) (e : Rn n), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → TendstoUniformlyOn (fun (d : ℝ) (x : Rn n) => d⁻¹ • (g (x + d • e) - g x)) (fun x => fderiv ℝ g x e) (𝓝[≠] 0) K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof: uniform convergence of difference quotients on a compact set, via uniform continuity of the derivative on a compact thickening and the mean value inequality. It is stated here for a general real normed codomain E, which is needed for the L(R^n,R^l)-valued map Dv. This is the argument of the accepted sibling-branch lemma Submission.dohr_eb_dql_diffQuot_tendstoUniformlyOn (codomain Rn l), which uses nothing about the codomain beyond its normed-space structure; its Lean proof (commit 33d90ae6) transfers verbatim with Rn l replaced by E.
1. Compact thickening. K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is ε > 0 with K_ε := cthickening ε K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). K_ε is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; R^n is proper).
2. Regularity. g is C^1 on the open set U, so g is differentiable at every z ∈ U (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≠ 0, and U ∈ 𝓝 z), and Dg is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). Hence Dg is uniformly continuous on the compact set K_ε ⊆ U (Heine–Cantor, IsCompact.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous).
3. Choice of constants. Let η > 0 (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff). By step 2, choose θ > 0 with ‖Dg(w) − Dg(z)‖ < η/(‖e‖ + 1) whenever w, z ∈ K_ε and |w − z| < θ. The set of d with 0 < |d| < min(ε, θ)/(‖e‖ + 1) is eventual for 𝓝[≠] 0, and every such d satisfies |d e| = |d| ‖e‖ ≤ |d| (‖e‖ + 1) < min(ε, θ).
4. Segment. Fix such d and x ∈ K. The segment [x, x + d e] lies in the closed ball B̄(x, |d e|), by convexity of balls. That ball lies in K_ε because |d e| < ε and x ∈ K (closedBall_subset_cthickening), so the segment lies in U. For w on the segment, |w − x| ≤ |d e| < θ and w, x ∈ K_ε, so ‖Dg(w) − Dg(x)‖ ≤ η/(‖e‖ + 1).
5. Mean value inequality. Apply the mean value inequality on the convex segment to g with the fixed linear map Dg(x) (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le'): ‖g(x + d e) − g(x) − Dg(x)(d e)‖ ≤ η/(‖e‖ + 1) · |d e|.
6. Division. Since d ≠ 0, Dg(x)e − d^{-1}(g(x + d e) − g(x)) = −d^{-1}(g(x + d e) − g(x) − Dg(x)(d e)). Its norm is at most |d|^{-1} · η/(‖e‖ + 1) · |d| ‖e‖ = η ‖e‖/(‖e‖ + 1) < η. This holds for every x ∈ K and every such d, so the difference quotients converge to x ↦ Dg(x)e uniformly on K along 𝓝[≠] 0. QED
Lean note: the proof is a single theorem using only the frozen imports. No options are needed: E is a type variable, and K_ε, Dg, segment and nhdsWithin are handled exactly as in the accepted proof.
proof_key_steps: compact thickening K_ε = cthickening ε K ⊆ U on which Dg is uniformly continuous (Heine–Cantor)
for 0 < |d| < min(ε,θ)/(‖e‖+1) the segment [x, x+de] lies in K_ε and ‖Dg(w) − Dg(x)‖ ≤ η/(‖e‖+1) on it
mean value inequality with the fixed linear map Dg(x): ‖g(x+de) − g(x) − Dg(x)(de)‖ ≤ η|de|/(‖e‖+1)
divide by |d|: ‖Dg(x)e − d⁻¹(g(x+de) − g(x))‖ < η uniformly for x ∈ K
